description:
Every developer task requires a different balance of quality, cost, and latency, but choosing a single AI model locks you into rigid trade-offs. Project HydraFusion is a research preview that introduces runtime orchestration to GitHub Copilot, automatically selecting the best execution path across multiple models. Learn how HydraFusion uses single, cascade, and critique workflows to optimize task completion without manual intervention. Explore how multi-model routing delivers frontier intelligence while reducing costs. 

Learn more: https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/?utm_source=youtube-launch-video&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=project-hydrafusion-sep-2026

author: GitHub
description:
Open source can feel intimidating when you’re staring at a mature repository with thousands of stars and no idea where to start.

In this episode of Open Source Friday, Andrea Griffiths sits down with Angela Wen, an engineer on GitHub’s Copilot platform, to walk through a first contribution from repository discovery to pull request.

They cover finding a `good first issue`, reading `README` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, forking and syncing a repository, creating a draft pull request, navigating CI checks, and setting realistic expectations with maintainers. They also discuss using Copilot responsibly. If you want another human to review your work, you need to read it first.

Stay through the end for a step-by-step beginner walkthrough. Then tell us: what was the first open source project you contributed to, and why?
title: Open Source Friday - Your first contribution to OSS
